events.title: ALGOL 58 preliminary report published
events.summary: Perlis and Samelson published the International Algebraic Language report in Communications of the ACM — later known as ALGOL 58.
events.about: ALGOL was designed as a portable algorithm notation for publishing and sharing programs across different computers. It influenced Pascal, C, and virtually every block-structured language that followed. Researchers used it to describe algorithms in journals without tying them to one machine's assembly code.

narrative.whyChosen: ALGOL 58 was the first major international effort to standardize how algorithms were written in print and code.
narrative.whyImportant: It established block structure, BNF-style rigor, and machine-independent thinking that shaped language design for decades.
narrative.problemSolved: Every computer had its own notation; scientists needed a common language to publish and compare algorithms.
